reviews.text: I usually finish more of a game before writing a review, but unfortunately I am leaving for vacation and only got to play this for an hour. I am leaving the positive review anyway because after even just an hour, I know this game is going to be well worth the purchase price. I have a lot of experience with rougelikes and also enjoy games on the more difficult side (my profile is public, see for yourself) and this game is surprisingly challenging - the boss designs are fun and engaging and are satisfying to kill. The meta progression is here in spades and you will absolutely feel more powerful as you unlock more upgrades and power boosts. The handling and flow of combat is probably the most important element for a game like this though, and I am pleased to say it feels GREAT! Very fluid and fast-paced, has a slick Ratchet and Clank vibe going for it and I am never bored, always on alert during most combat. Once you reach the second floor you will know this game does not mess around. All in all, this is a fantastic little rougelike shooter and I will be finishing it fully when I return from my vacation!

I've played the Demo, and I was curious where the Game would end up after its extra delay. The Game has a fascinating core concept, using Potions to enhance your arsenal. After all those four years of development, it's an impressive project, despite what else I will say in this review. If you like Ratchet & Clank-like games with cute Characters and that's enough, have fun. I personally give this Game an overall rating of about 5/10 at the moment, due to the many technical issues and lackluster gameplay. Honestly, for its price, it's alright. It's just a shame, because of the lack of polishing and questionable gameplay choices that hindered my enjoyment of the Game. I beat the Game in 2 hours on my second run, primarily using the fire shotgun. The developers had no contingency for that outcome and expect you to need many tries to beat the Game, making slow progress and thereby meeting all the Characters slowly. By winning this early, I've effectively skipped to the end of the Game and received the respect of all the other characters, who are still supposed to think that you suck. I'm not looking forward to playing again, because the System will still treat me like the fifty-exam-failure-dude that you are supposed to be, and ignore my success while the Characters are back to step one. Ironically, the Gameplay faces the usual conundrum with Potions in gaming: "I could use a potion right now, but what if I need it later?" While the overall movement is nice (besides getting stuck in the environment or your jump just not coming out), the potion mechanic is the core of the Game. So it hurts that it's underbaked. You can either drink, toss, or slot a potion into your gun. However, slotting it into your gun is generally the best option. Again, I've beaten the Game on the second run with basically only the fire shotgun. Because why bother tossing a potion for a one-time effect when you can get so much more value out of it as ammo. Drinking the Potion is also only suitable for certain potions. You also want to use your potions carefully, because you can quickly burn through them all. So, of course, you'll either try to use as few as possible or try to get as much value as possible. I really think that the whole Potion System could've been leagues better. Some are way better than others, or have only one use, which is a problem because you already have limited ingredients. Your customizability is rather bad as well. If you select multiple metal ingredients for the different potions, your opportunities to make potions become even more limited due to the random loot drops during a run. I think the Game would've benefited massively by taking more inspiration from Ratchet and Clank and adopting an Exp- or Enhancement System for the different potions, actually playing into the school aesthetic and incentivizing you to use your potions more to make them stronger because your Character learns how they work. It would've been far more rewarding to learn to use new ingredients instead of having to buy them from one of the students who's also notoriously bad at Alchemy. While still on Gameplay, the enemy animations and design are also somewhat confusing. Often, the attack indications are lacking or unclear, sometimes even false, like with the big lizard enemy in stage two, which has a bigger blast radius than indicated. Some attacks also feel like they have unfair timings. Some enemies immediately shoot you the moment they spawn, even though they're supposed to be in their spawning animation. The bosses feel like they're designed to surprise and overwhelm you in your first fights with them; for example, Akilah, the first Boss, is relatively newcomer-unfriendly, but I had the luck of Demo Experience. Lastly, you can fight your Rival (the first fight is mandatory), but the fight is over-tuned as she has about twice the health of even the final Boss. It took like 10 minutes of shooting, although perhaps the issue was that I couldn't yet load potions into my gun. So either Loading Potions into your guns is busted, or the Game legitimately expects you to spam that option, because it's simply the best tool you have. The other major Junk of the Game are the other Students you're supposed to befriend over your many attempts. If you like cute animal characters with simple but effective personalities, then you'll love them. They have lovely 2D portraits that perfectly fit their personalities (even though the teacher portraits feel like they have far too much detail and contrast with the simplistic 3D model). Some people called the 3D models uncanny, but I think they're charming. The real problem I have with the Characters is that if you're expecting more from them —like nuance —you're out of luck. After one interaction, you'll basically know exactly what they are about and what they're Story Arc will be about. In the Demo, I was already able to interact heavily with some of the Characters, and I didn't even think their Personal Arcs concluded satisfyingly (At least the ones I did). I admit I have to play some more so I can make more thorough thoughts. As for the rest of the Game, it's okay. The Campus is nice, but very empty and lifeless at the beginning. You have to unlock the Students one by one to see them on the Campus. The locations and visuals are good, though some textures seem buggy or have other issues. Characters constantly clip through their own clothing in their idle animations. The Music and Sound design is mediocre. It sadly feels like "Generic Fantasy Background Music" you'd type into YouTube for your DnD Session. As for the Sound Design, the overall mixing feels bad, with some rooms having no music at all or specific sound effects being way louder while others are very quiet. I've tried giving the game more chances but after literally softlocking me twice in a row, my enthusiasm is dead. It still has a lot of work put into it (And a lot of questionable advertising). It's honestly a reasonable price, too. So if you like it and can live with the flaws, that's great! And it seems to be the Studio's first Game. I just think it's a shame that there's so much polish still lacking and that some additional gameplay adjustments would've gone a long way. The initial start into the Game could even be off-putting for some people I think. I was looking forward to it, but sadly, I am disappointed.

[h1]炼金从打枪开始[/h1] 这是一个奇幻的世界，一个充满梦想与炼金的地方，你是这个世界炼金学院的学生，为了让自己变得更强，决定闯荡试炼之塔。你通过战胜塔中诸多怪物，获取炼金材料，以及炼金药水配方，越来越强。每一个关卡，就是一场考试，在一次次失败中，反复重来，最终通过所有的考试。 [h1]奇思妙想的炼金肉鸽[/h1] 《Brew 炼金学院物语》是一部奇幻炼金风格肉鸽游戏，我们将扮演炼金学院的一位学生，进入试炼之塔挑战，在其中不断的战胜敌人，获取炼金材料，以及炼金药水配方，让自己变得更加强大，从而通过一场场挑战，也就是一场场考试。 游戏的玩法为肉鸽刷塔关卡，进入一个个房间，战胜房间内所有敌人，最后获得宝箱，然后开出各种奖励。除去开奖励的宝箱外，还有一些特殊交互。比如购物货架，可以将身上炼金材料带出的炼金罐，这个可以带出的炼金材料是可以当做礼物送给NPC的。 游戏内的设计应有尽有，主地图偏向于一个小庭院，局外成长的职业流派，药水配方，以及可以试技能的小木偶，非常丰富，更是可以送NPC材料，以提高好感度，获得奖励。游戏的细节满满，画面柔和，视觉上比较享受。 [h1]总结[/h1] 游戏的风格偏向于油墨卡通，鲜艳的色彩，加上轻点的打击，使得操作十分顺滑，在进行近战和射击时非常流畅舒服。玩法比较休闲，人物机动性比较强，配合各种药剂，玩起来十分有趣。游戏可以休闲时间来上一把，娱乐一下。 [quote] 闲暇时光，不妨试试游戏。 欢迎关注[url=store.steampowered.com/curator/45653622/] 闲暇時光鉴赏组 [/url] [/quote]

[h3] 游戏简介[/h3] 这是一款战斗节奏紧凑的第三人称肉鸽游戏,战斗主要以fps为主，融合了npc日常养成和战斗元素，有较为丰富的玩法体验。 [h3] 玩法入门[/h3] 前期主要靠小手枪刮痧打怪，推荐使用键鼠操作，手柄不带自瞄操作起来很不舒服。游戏战斗的主要特色在于药瓶的使用，在游戏中杀怪、打碎建筑或者开箱子可以获取素材，通过2种素材可以合成一瓶药剂；药剂可以直接饮用来获得自身属性的提升和攻击特效，也可以装填到手枪中作为特殊弹药发出强力攻击，再就是可以当作手雷投掷出去。 强烈推荐强化引用水元素药剂，可以通过强化变为引用回血当血瓶用；再者就是投掷型雷元素药剂，扔出去以后可以形成一个雷暴区域，是一个大范围持续性aoe。 游戏中还加入了好感度养成系统，可以送礼提升高感度，好感度达到一定级别还有好礼相赠。 [h3] 缺点不足[/h3] 前期资源获取难度较大，刮痧非常严重，而且恢复手段非常少，需要较长时间来养成。 [h3]游戏画风不错，框架底子打磨的也不错，可以看作是小黑帝斯吧，推荐喜欢动作类肉鸽的玩家尝试[/h3] [quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44791929/]游戏好声音[/url]，认真品味好游戏，倾听游戏好声音。[/quote]

什么时候改好了什么时候改好评 1、开始界面鼠标变成羽毛笔判定有问题，明明放在要选的项目上了还得往左移1-2厘米才有反应 2、从草药学开始每一个战斗关时间也太长了吧，特别是每一小关都能碰上一两个那个草巨人，打完就给三五个瓶盖，纯负反馈 3、恢复手段特别局限，泉水也是幽默回复量，根本就不够回的，后面纯堆怪。第四次评论：点水的饮用回血，天赋拉每场战斗结束回血，土的套盾回血总算是够用了，天赋保命的盾牌和招架多点点出来过关就很容易了 4、动作在优化一下，太僵硬了 5、第二次评论：就在我打下这个评论再回到游戏的时候，给我卡死闪退了。。。 6、第三次评论：打一把游戏能给我卡退两次，第一次运气好他自己缓过来了，第二次又是黑屏闪退，你要干嘛？ 第四次评价：7、星象都点完得到猴年马月啊？打通一轮也就从8级升到10级 8、通过对话获得同学的喜好和厌恶有点慢了，我第8天就解锁了四个讨厌两个喜欢 9、后续看来望月镇还有boss，希望后面能去不同的地方闯关，不然那个地图放在那里也没啥用，还有船，最好也能去副本，通关之后也没有增加难度选项，有点无聊 10、每个帽子最好像hades的饰品一样有点有趣的效果 11、带出来的炼金物品最好除了送礼还有别的作用 12、谁能告诉我许愿井能干啥，纽特好感度从1-5都扔了一次也没见得有啥效果

有点：画面不错，背景设定不错，战斗打击感和反馈以及BOSS和小怪设计不错。 缺点：极其稀少的回血，在外面没有更多强化之前。前期只有打死一大关的BOSS之后有泉水，而且只给你补充最大生命值的30%。没错 一整6 7个小关卡都不会给你任何回复手段。而且你的血量初始很低 怪物和陷阱的伤害对前期的主角来说十分疼痛。这游戏就完全没打算让你在低养成阶段的时候就通关。作者根本不知道什么是Rogue游戏。他似乎以为玩家把外面的养成拉满 然后最终通关游戏一次，这才是Rogue游戏的玩法。但其实应该是玩家在对局中靠自己的努力通关的同时 顺带去养成局外内容，然后通过自己提高难度来获得更多奖励和更高难度的挑战。我第一次遇到一个恶意这么大的Rogue游戏……这游戏前面的几个优点完全是瑕不掩瑜。 我只能给到55分/100分。

[h1]一个小老鼠的故事——铁杵能磨成针[/h1] 在艾奇恩大陆上，有一座神秘的学院，在这里有着神奇的炼金术，每年，这座学院吸引着全国各地的学生前来。 今天，你终于成为了学院的一员，不是天赋多高，不是身世显赫。 而是，你竟然参加了50次！！！！终于学院被打动了，你正式成为学院的一员，今天，我们的故事将从这里开始。 [h2]小老鼠成长史[/h2] 在学院都是猫的世界中，作为小老鼠，当然很多同学都是恶意满满。而最好让他们闭嘴的方式，就是通关试炼之塔！！ 可以说，游戏的核心都是至始至终围绕试炼之塔展开的。 在试炼之塔的挑战中，主角很灵活，手持一把手枪，还可以进行近战攻击。 在每一个个单个组成的房间中，击败怪物，开启宝箱。 过程中，玩家会获得各种材料，而这些材料，就是后续合成药水的关键。 那么，游戏怎么玩呢？我先下个结论，我觉得是药水！ 可能有玩家问，药水是什么？且听我细细道来。 游戏初期，药水分为火系、水系药水，后续会陆续解锁风系、雷系、冰系、土系。 喝下药水后，会带来属性增强，比如火属性，喝下后就可以让武器附带火属性。 比如水系，喝下就是水的效果。 除去直接服用，玩家还可以将药水投掷，火系就会形成一摊像岩浆一样的效果。风系就会将敌人吹起来。 另外还可以在商店中解锁将药水装进武器里，装上又是另一种效果。 火系像散弹一样，水系像弹弹球一样，很有意思。 打的过程中，我感觉就是秒造药水，然后装备，接着打打打，前期还好，到关卡boss，不仅要快速制作，还得不断闪避。 [h2]游戏的优点在哪里？[/h2] 画面和风格我特别喜欢，卡通风格为主，在配以各种动物元素。 包括游戏里的怪物，多数都是机械改造的，攻击方式都是带特效的，要不就是吐泡泡，要不就是带粉色的尾巴冲刺。 还有游戏内的各种角色，有好感度可以养成，通过送礼，提升好感度。 同时，还有不同的事件进行遭遇，你的每一次选择，都将决定和该角色的关系。 另外，游戏过程中，你会收获不同的徽章，带有不同的属性，什么多收集材料，什么加中毒，什么加护甲。 还有随机出现的回血的泉水，物品多多的大宝箱，解锁药水的房间，还有不同药水的天赋树，让你的相关药水变得更强。 整体体验下来，《Brew 炼金学院物语》作为一款第三人称肉鸽游戏，卡通的风格，多变的关卡。 不失为一款有趣的游戏，友情提示，前期具有一定的难度，需要耐心哦！ [quote]欢迎关注『 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45525570/] 桃你欢心 [/url]』 [b] 桃影扶风评百戏，落墨如歌写人间[/b][/quote]
玩法机制还是可以的，希望有更多的新内容（新药水、新配方、剧情以及新地图）； 前期有点牢，但等级上去星象天赋点满还是可以爽爽的； 动作还得优化一下、准星设置也得加，没配音有点逗； bug和优化问题修完几次后少了，但还是有； 刷npc的好感度也有点阴间，部分角色喜欢和讨厌的礼物得一个一个的去尝试； 总之，游戏的底子还是不错的，就是各方面需要打磨和完善。

Y'all, I'm really torn on this. I *want* to be able to recommend this game. Maybe in a month or two? It's "released" but it doesn't feel ready for release, it still feels like it's in playtesting. Almost everything I like about this game is actually the art and design. This game is beautiful looking. The lighting, shading, character designs. I want to engage with it all more. But the biggest reason I can't recommend this game is the amount of bugs/frankly just unfinished game design I've encountered. 75 minutes of gameplay, I've encountered bugs like graphical glitches, text in UI going off screen, needing to reset cause I was stuck in dialogue, one-sided texture so you can see through it on the other side, UI appearing and disappearing quickly at the start of a run and making me think it glitched out and I missed something (but it's really just that the UI becomes relevant when you've played the game more.) I think the audio mixing is pretty imbalanced. Sound effects are extremely quiet, even after turning them up (they were set to half the music volume by default.) The gun sound is fine, but there's almost no footstep/dash sound, and the melee sound is dissatisfying. Enemies are extremely quiet as well. It kind of feels like playing a game with sound effects turned off, honestly? There's no game-over music, so the boss music just kept playing after I lost, which felt odd. There's plenty of animations that still need polishing, the first boss felt kind of janky. The player character sits down every so often, kind of randomly, not even after being idle for a bit; I mention this because there is no animation for him getting up, he kind of just splits from sitting to running instantly. When you enter the tower, your character just kind of plops down. It feels like he goes from floating in the air idle to landing on the ground, which is weird. Gameplay wise, it's okay I guess? Don't play it with a controller like I did for starters. It's a shooter, it wants you to use a mouse. You have a default gun, but can change the type of gun you're using by loading it with potions. It's just not that exciting. It doesn't actually change your gameplay that much. You aim and shoot. You have a dash, but there's not much movement involved. It felt like I was just strafing and aiming. When chests and enemies drop currencies, you have to move close to it to pick it up, which feels pretty bad. Open chest, wait a couple seconds to make sure you get all the loot, then continue. I beat enemies during a boss fight and realized I'd have to wander all over the arena to pick up everything they dropped. Overall, a lot of standard roguelite fair, and sadly I mean that in a not-so-great way here. The loot and upgrades are relatively vanilla. "You get a double-jump." or "You have a 30% chance to not take damage." or "Your melee now applies poison." The melee attack isn't satisfying, you bounce off destructibles after punching them and it only destroys one. The cooldown on melee doesn't feel good and should probably be replaced with a wind-up before or wind-down animation after punching. Having to watch the melee icon to see when I can melee again feels weird and artificial. I've played Risk of Rain 2 & Hades, just to name a couple obvious roguelites. I don't think games like this should inherently be addictive, but I'm not actually *excited* to play. I think my biggest incentive is to see more art and characters and dialogue, but the lack of ambience, no character voice sounds on dialogue, dissatisfying audio mixing, and generally uninteresting gameplay leaves me unenthused. At the very least, I'd like to see a lot of these bugs fixed. Better audio design would be nice. A gameplay revamp would be amazing. I could at least say the game feels properly playtested if most of the bugs were fixed; but I'm still not sure the art & design is enough to recommend the game. Truly wanna see this game do well, but it needs to be a little deeper, gameplay wise. Good luck.

Can't recommend at current state, -Shooting and punching feels very unsatisfying, everything feels like sponge. -80% of items/buffs in the dungeon are temporary/consumables, hard to feel progress. -Different base materials are annoying, if I pick copper for every potion, crafting is a lot smoother. Shouldn't they encourage players to use different potion buffs? -Healing is very limited, you just can't take damage. You get 15 heal at the end of the stage, and 20% heal very randomly from chests. Isn't it a bit too much? -Every character model looks decent expect for the protagonist for some reason(that shocked face still haunting me).

Brew in UEVR is very promising. This one works very well in deed. The visuals look amazing, and personally I love games that have this bright, colorful, appealing look to them. It shows promise as one of the bestter experiences to be played in VR. There seems to be a good amount to explore in the hub world, but right now my attempts to go into battle have been thwarted before completing much... [h1][b]掌控药水的大师[/b][/h1] 《炼金学院物语》是一款非常有趣的肉鸽游戏，作为炼金学院的新生，角色可以灵活的运用各种药水，以元素之力在试炼之塔中一路前行。 本作是一款第三人称弹幕肉鸽游戏，画面以卡通风呈现，视觉表现还可以。 游戏的玩法便是典型的肉鸽闯关，通过炼金与构筑在一个又一个战斗关卡中冒险，和《哈迪斯》一样，期间可以选择下个房间的类型。 角色持有一把手枪，默认载弹6发，有无限备弹，手感的话有点软绵绵的，且没有开镜瞄准，因此需要简单适应一下。 游戏的精彩之处是各种神奇的药水，每种药水都有不同的配方，通过杀敌、打碎场景中物品等可以获取素材，随后按下TAB即可一键制作。 药水有多种用途： - 按Q可以饮用，角色一段时间内会获得buff增强，比如提升移速。 - 按右键可以掷出，由于是一次性消耗的，效果比较强大，比如造成大范围爆炸、将敌人浮空等。 - 按R键可以装填进枪里，这会改变枪械的输出模式，比如火系药水对应霰弹枪、风系药水对应狙击枪等。 这套设计非常的有创意，玩家可以根据当前场景或是自己的风格灵活使用，还能和构筑进一步搭配。 构筑方面则是经典的三选一了，游戏允许按照药水的类型来增强，效果诸如弹药命中时产生爆炸、近战攻击时留下燃烧区域等。 非常有意思的一款游戏，赋予了药水诸多特性，将这一传统游戏中的消耗品变成了核心所在，能加强下手感和操控就好了，值得一试。 [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]

Cute game. The main character looks... pretty gross, but the gameplay is simple and cute. I have two main issues that will probably get fixed in time. 1) The lightning gun is insanely broken. It carries you through the whole game, with more ammo compared to firing time than any other gun before you even upgrade it. It's a beam that does low damage repeatedly, and occasionally discharges to hit all nearby enemies. The problem is the badges. 10% chance to poison, 10% chance to crit and everything to do with rage giving more attack speed and movement speed means this thing outdamages every other slow firing weapon. 2) Only getting one NPC event per return to the academy is really annoying. I levelled up multiple NPCs affection at the same time, so I had to reload the hub multiple times so every character's event would work normally. Other than that, the NPCs are the best part of this game. It has a mechanic similar to Hades where you can give them gifts, but unlike Hades where it is just a single gift you can give to anyone, you need to find out what each NPC likes, and that's really smart and enjoyable. Rebalance the lightning gun and fix the main character's gross rat face (Rats can be really cute, but not like this) and this is an absolute little gem of a game.

A cartoonish furry school simulator aesthetic on a ranged roguelite, it's pretty solid. There's a couple weird janky bugs and odd balance, but the latter is kinda hard to notice if you aren't paying attention. Some of the animations and combat are great, but some are a little lacking. All of the characters are pretty adorable, but the static poses and faces can be uncanny at times. I get it's kinda low budget in that regard, but specifically the protagonist has the dopiest expression and look about him, especially when he's grinning. Every character kinda does this, but to a much lesser extent than the protag. The story is pretty typical, but the writing is sometimes basic and meh. There's some interesting world building and background to the characters, but I'm not sure it leads to a lot. Sadly, there is no voice acting. I think it would've been funny to hear Cinnabitch constantly talking trash and raging at you. Combat is pretty fun. Your base gun is not bad, and I found myself alternating using it in tandem with potion weapons. At first, potions seem like a very precious resource, and it kind of is, but the later stages really add a heavy emphasis on trying to round yourself in combat. Between specializing aspects of different potions (which can be annoyingly RNG in a few layers), you can focus on using weapons, throws, or consumable effects, with all of them being different. You can rapidly craft in the middle of combat, and use different potions in different ways rapidly. For example: A ton of enemies spawn and surround me, and it looks bad. I can drink a water potion for high speed maneuvering, and then craft a lightning potion to try and chain attacks. Or throw a fire potion, and finish them off with a water potion gun. You're not meant to use the same setup run to run, since you don't have much control over whatever specialization you end up with, but the guns all served a decent purpose. I liked the air rifle for sniping, and taking out tough enemies and bosses, but I used the hell out of my base potion gun to preserve potions, and used my potion weapons when they'd be more effective. This is, without a doubt, the best part of the game (once you can roll resources, and start budgeting and dispensing as needed). It makes the boss fights much better. iFrame dodging is a thing, and pretty important to the gameplay, too. In case anyone wanted to know, it has a cooldown, and there is no stamina function attached. You can get an extra dash through an Agility badge, and maybe reduced cooldown (idr), but I didn't have those on my first clear, and badges are things you pick up for a run--not permanent upgrades. Animations overall are solid and lively, and the world is colorful and cartoony for an appropriate aesthetic. Seasons sometimes change for the academy, but the rooms can be bland at times. I think there needs to be a little more detail in them with objects or lights, or something. It's just a bit sparse for my taste, even in the academy sometimes, where NPCs sometimes wander around, but mostly just idle in varying places. Difficulty: Hard starting out. Kind of expected, and most roguelites vary on this. There's various progressions, and some of it is tied to the affection with characters. This is because you can unlock ingredients through them, which can be used as a choice on how certain potions function. This isn't really a problem, since the base ingredients for all of them are perfectly fine (and generally my preferred anyway). It's just kinda odd, I guess, but I beat the game without unlocking all the potions, or even all the characters. There is a skill tree, which is very impacting, and where grinding your inevitable win will be. Normally, I pick up the healing nodes when learning a game, but I ended up beating my first run with the bonus stardust (level up/skill currency), and some weapon nodes instead, and had an okay-ish set of badges. More than anything, it was just playing my butt off, and really leaning into the various potions and the effects I specialized in. This is what makes it an enjoyable challenge to me. Post-game has 'Ambition' which is like Heat from Hades, or extra challenge parameters, and the bottom one you can set is to disable your skill tree. I can't even imagine. lol Some enemies have some pretty crazy attacks (ultra fast dashes, especially in the Biology portion), and Melee weaving--which is very powerful--can be super risky, and sometimes not worth it. Strategically speaking, it was great to use this, but you have to observe and learn the enemies to find out when it's safe to combo this in. There's some pretty great badges for this, but you can avoid them and just try to lean on your guns and alchemy if you don't want to bother. The game does have a bit of a rating system based on your time (unsure if other metrics affect it). I didn't seem to struggle with getting a decent grade, but I'm sure running all A+ is possible with some good RNG, player skill, and the skill tree. I wasn't far off on my first completion, and that was around 4 hours in (felt kinda like a lucky run, for the most part). I ran into a bug with the Water Potion dodge resulting in animation locking, Dash having a temporarily frozen cooldown, and my basic shot being disabled a few times, as well as my directional--seems tied to the elixir accept screen in the middle of combat. Rare, and not lethal, but you can take several hits completely out of your control. I don't know why the exact trigger for this is the way it is, as most of the time I could hold an air rifle shot with it, so it might be tied to trying to fire or reload the base gun as you dash, too. Recommend: If you're into the aesthetic and gameplay, it can be pretty fun. It's not a high budget game, but it's solid with the combat through the various options in alchemy; multiple guns to activate, throw effects, drinking effects, and badges. Though my main PC is a 7800X3D / 4090, my backup PC (which I recently used to travel) ran this with medium graphics just fine on an i7-8700k / GTX 1070 Ti at 1440p, 120 FPS.
